title: Tenths: The First Rung Below One

steps.body: You already climbed the ×10 ladder up to a million: each rung left is ten times bigger. Now climb the other way. Split one whole into 10 equal parts and each part is a **tenth** — the first rung *below* the ones place. We write one tenth as **0.1**, and the dot (the decimal point) marks where the ones place ends.
A tenth is one of ten equal steps.

widget.prompt: Place 0.7 on the line from 0 to 1.
widget.successFeedback: Seven steps of one tenth. The gap from 0 to 1 is cut into ten, and 0.7 is the seventh mark — decimals are just a finer set of rungs on the same ladder.
widget.lowFeedback: Your marker is below 0.7 — you have taken fewer than 7 tenths.
widget.highFeedback: Your marker is above 0.7 — you have taken more than 7 tenths.

predict.prompt: Before you place it: is 0.7 closer to 0 or to 1?
predict.reveal: 0.7 sits 0.7 from 0 and 0.3 from 1 — the 1 side wins. Judging position from the endpoints first makes the exact placement easier to defend.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents tenths intro.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for tenths intro must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines tenths intro.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 0.7 means 7 out of 10 equal parts — the fraction 7/10.
The tenths digit is the numerator over a denominator of 10.

options.feedback: 7/100 would be 0.07, seven hundredths. A single digit after the point is tenths: 0.7 = 7/10.
1/7 isn't a tenth at all. 0.7 means 7 of the 10 equal parts: 7/10.
7 is the whole number seven. 0.7 is less than one — seven tenths, or 7/10.

steps.body: The ladder rule still holds, both directions: the ones place is **ten times** one tenth, and one tenth is **one tenth of** the ones place. So 0.1 × 10 = 1, and 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1. Tenths are just the ladder's next rung down.

explanationVariants: Since one tenth is 1÷10, stacking ten of them returns to 1.

widget.prompt: How many tenths make one whole?

commonErrors.feedback: 1 tenth is just one part. It takes 10 of those parts to rebuild the whole: 10 tenths = 1.
100 is how many hundredths make a whole — a smaller rung. Ten tenths make one whole.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The whole was split into 10 equal parts, so it takes all 10 to rebuild it.

steps.body: Match each decimal to its fraction.

widget.prompt: Match each tenths decimal to its fraction.

pairErrors.feedback: 6/10 is 0.6, not 0.9. The tenths digit is the numerator: 0.9 pairs with 9/10.

widget.missFeedback: The single digit after the point is the numerator, over a denominator of 10.
widget.successFeedback: 0.3=3/10, 0.9=9/10, 0.6=6/10 — the tenths digit is always the numerator.

explanationVariants: More shaded tenths means a bigger decimal: 0.3 < 0.5 < 0.7.
Comparing tenths is just comparing the single digits after the point.

widget.prompt: Which lists 0.3, 0.7, and 0.5 from LEAST to greatest?

options.feedback: Comparing the tenths digits 3<5<7 orders them correctly.
That's greatest to least — the reverse. Least first is 0.3, 0.5, 0.7.
0.3 is smaller than 0.5, so it comes first. Least to greatest: 0.3, 0.5, 0.7.
0.5 is smaller than 0.7, so it comes before it. Least to greatest: 0.3, 0.5, 0.7.

hints: A dime is one tenth of a dollar — 0.1 of a dollar.
Write seven tenths as a decimal.
explanationVariants: Each dime is 1/10 of a dollar, so 7 dimes is 7/10 = 0.7 of a dollar.
Seven tenths of a dollar is written 0.7.

widget.prompt: A dime is one tenth of a dollar. Written as a decimal of a dollar, how much is 7 dimes? Enter the tenths digit (the ? in 0.?).

commonErrors.feedback: 70 would be 70 tenths — far more than a dollar. Seven dimes is 7 tenths: 0.7, digit 7.
10 is how many dimes make a whole dollar, not the count here. Seven dimes is 0.7.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each dime is 0.1; seven of them is 7 tenths.

takeaways: Splitting one whole into 10 equal parts makes tenths; one tenth is written 0.1.
The single digit after the decimal point is the tenths digit — and the numerator over 10.
steps.teaser: next: two more rungs down — hundredths and thousandths.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **One tenth is one of 10 equal parts of a whole, written 0.1.** If 3 of the 10 parts are shaded, that's 3 tenths — the decimal 0.3, or the fraction 3/10.

explanationVariants: The shaded count out of 10 is the tenths digit.

widget.prompt: 5 of 10 equal parts are shaded. As a decimal, that's:

options.feedback: 5.0 is the whole number five. 5 out of 10 parts is 5 tenths: 0.5.
0.05 is five hundredths, a smaller rung. 5 of 10 parts is 5 tenths: 0.5.
